svg.text: flat cut-outs living in a subsector, drawn after its walls, clipped by the same span list — and closing it behind themselves
THE GREEN ARMOUR · POSE (-104,-3232,128) · THE SPAN SET AS REAL TRAPEZIA, BEFORE AND AFTER THE OBJECT
the object is drawn AFTER its subsector's walls, and it closes columns like a wall does — only on its BOT side
columns 101→155 now bounded by the lid arc
the aperture reaches the floor: one wide trapezium
the billboard is not in the list yet — it is about to put itself there
ten thin trapezia now trace the armour's own silhouette
Every one is BOT side: a cut-out blocks what is below
its top edge and nothing above it. Only the lid arc is
allowed to tighten; the outline draws with it switched off,
so the figure can never clip itself.
→ a gap remains, so the object is built at all
ONE BILLBOARD, STEP BY STEP · EVERY COUNT FROM THIS FRAME
LEVEL OF DETAIL · REAL ART AT REAL SIZES · THE SHAPE IS SWAPPED, NOT SCALED
One byte per kind sets the switch. Doubling the distance at which a hoplite gains detail was a one-byte edit: 15 → 7.
17 of 37 stamped billboards over the corpus were fully occluded:
53,816 cycles that drew nothing. That is why step 7 exists.
objects are 9.9% of the render suite · six slots a subsector · nearest first · one occlusion question can retire a whole slot · only the lid arc tightens
